title: asian stocks draw foreign buyers after nine month selloff 2026 09 10
text:
Sept 10 (Reuters) - Foreign investors returned to net buying of Asian stocks in August, ending a nine-month selling streak as AI-linked tech stocks attracted buyers following a ​sharp July selloff and a strong earnings season.
Foreign investors bought a ‌net $4.72 billion of stocks in Taiwan, South Korea, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines last month, according to LSEG data. They added a further $1.52 billion to regional equities ​through Tuesday's close this month.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS)
, opens new tab
 ​rose 3.01% last month from a 3-1/2-month low of 797.6 ⁠in July, as upbeat guidance from Amazon (AMZN.O)
, opens new tab
, Microsoft (MSFT.O)
, opens new tab
 and Nvidia (NVDA.O)
, opens new tab
 pointed to strong demand for regional ​tech exporters.
Asian companies beat analysts' earnings estimates by an average 10.2% in the ​latest quarter, posting 44.7% year-on-year profit growth, while the technology sector recorded growth of 88.3%, LSEG data for 2,108 large- and mid-cap companies showed.
"The latest foreign inflows appear to reflect ​a renewed AI allocation rather than a broad-based return to Asia," said ​Song Zhe, a senior investment specialist for Asia ex-Japan and global emerging market equities at ‌BNP Paribas ⁠Asset Management.
Foreign investors bought a net $11.15 billion of Taiwanese stocks last month, ending a two-month selling streak. South Korean stocks, however, recorded a fourth consecutive monthly outflow, totalling $8.65 billion.
So far this month, foreign investors have added $1.1 billion to ​South Korean stocks and $1.45 ​billion to Taiwanese ⁠shares.
Foreign investors also bought a net $3.1 billion of Indian stocks in August, marking a second straight month of net ​purchases.
Indonesian and Vietnamese stocks attracted inflows of $68 million and $11 million, ​respectively, while ⁠Thai and Philippine equities saw outflows of $749 million and $216 million.
"The return of the AI trade, improving technology earnings and cleaner positioning should favour North Asia, particularly Taiwan ⁠and ​selected Korean technology companies," BNP Paribas' Zhe said.
"Higher ​bond yields, oil prices and geopolitical risks may keep markets volatile, so we favour visible earnings upgrades ​and direct exposure to AI infrastructure."
